input.question: Is there evidence that incest leads to genetic deformities? If so, how was it tested? What was the sample size / p-value / confidence interval? Was the claim held up to less scrutiny because this is a common belief?
input.ground_truth: We actually know a lot about inbreeding do to its importance in laboratory test animals and agriculture. The reason incest leads to genetic deformities is that those genes are usually recessive and they can only appear if the mother and father both possess the gene. Obviously related individuals are for likely to share the same negative recessive genes. I'm on mobile so I can't find exact studies but hopefully someone else can point you in the right direction.

Okay, let’s try to explain this in a very simple way, like I’m talking to a 5-year-old:

Imagine you have a big family tree with lots of cousins and aunts and uncles. Sometimes, people in stories or in real life talk about people who are very close in the family having a baby together. Some people say that if this happens, the baby might have problems because of their genes.

Scientists wanted to see if this is true. They looked at lots and lots of families and babies to see if babies from very close family members (like siblings or parents and children) had more health problems than babies from families that weren’t so close.

They checked many babies—maybe hundreds or thousands—to see if there was a pattern. They used numbers to see if the difference was real and not just by chance. They looked at things like how often problems happened and used special numbers called “p-values” to see if the difference was big enough to trust.

But it’s a tricky thing to study, and sometimes people already believe something, so they might not look at the facts as carefully. But scientists try to be careful and look at the facts.

What they found is that when people who are very closely related have a baby, there is a higher chance that the baby might have some health problems. But it doesn’t happen to every baby, and it’s not super common because it’s not very common for close family members to have babies together.

So, yes, there is some evidence from big studies, but it’s a rare thing, and scientists try to look at the facts carefully, even if it’s a belief lots of people have.
